newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran MP urges halt to investments in east Germany.
newsitem.headline: Iran MP urges halt to investments in east Germany.

text.p: Iran's deputy speaker of parliament on Sunday urged the government to suspend investment plans in eastern Germany, the first such call since a German court accused Iran's leaders of ordering political killings.
Tehran radio said Hassan Rowhani, speaking at a scheduled parliament session, demanded the government "cancel investments in the east of Germany".

It said Rowhani also demanded that Iran should seek a compensation of 18 billion marks ($10.5 billion) for the failure of German companies to finish building a nuclear power plant in Iran after Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution.
German officials had said last year that Iran was interested in buying some troubled east German companies in the former Communist region in an effort to improve ties with Bonn.

Iran on Saturday said it would recall its ambassadors from European Union states who have summoned their Tehran envoys after Thursday's German court verdict said Iranian leaders had ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish opposition figures. Iran has denied any role in the killings.
